news.headline: Pakistan requests $6.7bn Saudi deferred-payment oil facility, plans 45-day strategic petroleum reserve, pitches Gwadar 'Maritime Energy City' to Gulf states
news.summary: Dawn's Business & Finance Weekly (published Jul 20, 2026): Pakistan currently 'operates largely on a fragile, just-in-time commercial inventory model' for petroleum stocks; government plans a 45-day emergency oil buffer in an initial phase, with a longer-term objective of expanding to 90-day capacity, and is promoting development of a 'Pakistan Maritime Energy City' at Gwadar Port inviting Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to establish and maintain strategic crude-oil reserves there, which would grant Pakistan first-purchase rights during an emergency. Separately, Pakistan formally requested a $6.7 billion deferred-payment oil facility from Saudi Arabia carrying a 1% interest rate, 15-year repayment period and 5-year grace period, an improvement on a previous $1.2bn facility (6% interest) agreed in February 2025 that expired in April. Article contains no specific mention of PSX-listed OMCs or refiners (PSO, ATRL, NRL, PRL) and no confirmation that the Saudi facility or Gulf reserve-storage arrangement has been finalised - logged as impact 3 (relevant, moderate) pending confirmation of any signed agreement.

No financial figure for the contribution disclosed in the source reviewed - reputational/CSR item, not financial.

news.summary: Zindigi, powered by JS Bank Limited (JSBL), was recognised as Pakistan's Best Digital Bank at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence; Zindigi Chief Officer Noman Azhar quoted: 'Pakistan deserves digital financial experiences that stand alongside the very best in the world, not just the best in Pakistan.' No financial figures disclosed - reputational/award item, not financial; picked up this cycle via Dawn's Jul 20 Company News column referencing the same award.

news.headline: PSX surges over 2,000 points intraday on Middle East mediation news, then pares gains
news.summary: Tuesday session (this checkpoint), from previous confirmed close of 175,927.73: Pakistan Today reported the KSE-100 up over 2,000 points in early trade as oil prices eased; Business Recorder had the index at 177,967.47 at 10:58am, up 2,039.74 points (+1.16%), then at 177,121.97 by 1:30pm, up 1,194.24 points (+0.68%) as the early gain pared back; Express Tribune reported a further intraday read of 177,023.97 (high 178,370.45, low 176,930.74), volume 221.59m shares, value Rs13.63bn traded at that point. Driver per all three: improved investor sentiment on reports of mediation efforts between the US and Iran, easing oil prices, alongside anticipation of the earnings season; buying observed in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil & gas exploration companies, OMCs and power generation, with index-heavy HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, PPL, POL, HBL, MEBL, MCB and NBP trading in the green intraday. No sector/stock-level closing-bell narrative article located in sources reviewed this cycle to confirm the final print (see separate PSX-official confirmed-close entry logged this cycle).

news.headline: OGRA daily fuel pricing: petrol cut Re0.35 to Rs315.80/litre, diesel raised Rs5.71 to Rs360.06/litre
news.summary: Effective July 21, 2026, under OGRA's new daily (rather than fortnightly) pricing mechanism introduced July 17, 2026: petrol price decreased by Re0.35 per litre to Rs315.80/litre; high-speed diesel (HSD) price increased by Rs5.71 per litre to Rs360.06/litre. Per the sources reviewed, OGRA now works out rates using the average international oil price of the previous seven days and announces revised prices every working day (Monday-Friday), with weekend prices held flat; other fiscal components (Petroleum Development Levy, customs duty, climate levy, OMC margins) remain government-controlled. Smaller, incremental daily move under the new mechanism versus the large fortnightly hikes logged earlier this month (e.g. the +Rs13.18/+Rs13.80 hike on Jul 11) - relevant for OMC (PSO) and refiner (ATRL, NRL, PRL) margins and for headline inflation, but not a shock-magnitude move.

news.headline: Profit repatriation by foreign investors rises 4pc in FY26 to $2.305bn
news.summary: Per SBP data reported by Business Recorder: foreign companies operating in Pakistan repatriated $2.305bn in profits and dividends during FY2025-26, up from $2.219bn in FY2024-25 (+$86m, +4%); 95.5% of the amount was returns on FDI and 4.5% from FPI; the United Kingdom was the largest destination for repatriation at $621.2m, followed by China at $486.5m; financial services was the largest contributing sector at $523.2m, followed by power at $478.2m. Background macro data point on external-account flows, no individual PSX-ticker figures disclosed.

news.headline: SBP likely to keep interest rate unchanged at 11.5% at July 27 MPC meeting, survey shows
news.summary: Published Jul 21, 2026: a Topline Securities survey found 97% of market participants expect the State Bank of Pakistan's Monetary Policy Committee to hold the policy rate at 11.5% when it meets July 27, 2026 (only 3% expect a 100bps cut), citing heightened geopolitical uncertainty and the recent rebound in international oil prices despite contained inflation; the SBP last reviewed policy on June 15, 2026, also holding at 11.5%. About 49% of respondents expect the rate to remain at 11.5% by December 2026 while 46% foresee further easing; Topline Research itself expects the rate to fall below 11.5% by year-end. This is a market-expectation survey ahead of the decision, not the decision itself - logged as impact 3 (notable/guidance) pending the actual MPC outcome on July 27.

news.headline: Pakistan seeks $10 billion US exchange stabilisation facility to bolster forex reserves
news.summary: Reported Jul 21-22, 2026 (Reuters exclusive, citing a source): Pakistan has formally requested a $10 billion bilateral exchange stabilization facility from the US Treasury (addressed to US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent), with a maturity of up to five years, aimed at strengthening forex reserves, supporting the rupee and reducing reliance on multilateral lenders; the request followed Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb's meeting with Bessent in Washington on Tuesday (Jul 21). Pakistan remains under its existing $7 billion IMF programme. Not yet approved/finalised by the US side per sources reviewed - logged as impact 3 (relevant, moderate) pending confirmation of any agreement.

news.headline: Brent crude tops $92/bbl, nearly six-week high, as Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea blockade and US strikes Iran for 10th straight day
news.summary: Published Jul 22, 2026: Brent crude trading at $92.71/bbl (TradingEconomics), up 1.87% on the day and its highest level in nearly six weeks; separate wire figures cited Brent above $92/bbl generally. Drivers: the US carried out a 10th consecutive day of strikes against Iran after President Trump vowed Tehran 'will pay' for attacks that killed American soldiers, and separately dismissed the likelihood of imminent US-Iran talks while warning of further strikes; a Kuwaiti-flagged tanker carrying oil products was struck near the Strait of Hormuz; Yemen's Houthi militants threatened to blockade Saudi Arabia's maritime traffic in the Red Sea, emailing shipowners advising against calling at Saudi ports, with at least three tankers already reported to have U-turned in the southern Red Sea; the US pledged retaliation if the Houthis disrupt Red Sea shipping; Saudi Arabia is rerouting crude via pipelines to cut reliance on the Strait of Hormuz; separately, attacks on the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal on Russia's Black Sea coast are disrupting Kazakhstan's crude exports. Sharp, multi-corridor commodity/supply-risk move per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10) - direct read-through for Pakistan's OMC (PSO), refiners (ATRL, NRL, PRL), E&P names (MARI, OGDC, PPL), gas utilities (SNGP, SSGC) and HUBC, plus renewed inflation/import-bill and current-account pressure economy-wide; escalation flagged.
